sahneler.metin: During a test flight, Virgin Galactic's SpaceShipTwo broke apart.
Within seconds, it disintegrated, killing the co-pilot.
The pilot survived after being thrown clear.
Its tail feathered to slow it for re-entry.
The co-pilot unlocked that system too early, near the speed of sound.
Air loads forced the tail up on their own.
Nothing in the design prevented that single error.
An automatic lock was added to stop early unlocking.

aciklama:
SpaceShipTwo broke apart during a powered test flight. The cause: aerodynamic loads deploying the tail feather after an early unlock, with no inhibit to prevent it.
